method: I mapped all 295 catalog ids to their CommandSpec run functions in crates/engine/src/cmd/*.rs (the gc*/dc* ids come from the gc!/dc! macros in constraints.rs) and read each, then grepped the engine and the crates it calls (doc, geom, render, fonts, constraints, io, dwg, dxf) for std::fs, std::env, std::process, std::net, clipboard crates and nested Session::execute/cmdline/script calls. Only run_open, save_to (qsave/saveas), run_wblock and run_plot (plot/exportpdf) touch paths; every nested execute targets a fixed safe command (explode, properties.set, dist, area, layout.set); nothing persists Session.settings, uses the OS clipboard, a device or the network, or runs scripts (Session::script and Session::cmdline, which run arbitrary commands, are reached only by the MCP `script` tool and the CLI, outside this catalog). File commands are classified as if the host's IoHooks were installed, which OctoSense's cad service never does (open {path} still reads the file before noticing). Known limit: text-style replies and text rendering read installed system fonts by family name from fixed font folders, which I kept safe because no caller path is involved.

rules.why: run_open reads `path` with std::fs::read and only then hands the bytes to open_bytes, which needs the host's IoHooks.read (cadcraft_io::read: DXF, or DWG through acadrust). So even in OctoSense's cad service, which installs no hooks, `open {path}` reads any readable file and its error says whether the path exists; `{data, name}` takes base64 bytes and touches no path.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs: run_open calls std::fs::read(path) before open_bytes checks io()
crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs: IoHooks/set_io, installed only by apps/cadcraft, apps/cadcraft-cli and apps/cadcraft-web
crates/io/src/lib.rs: read() parses bytes only (DWG via cadcraft_dwg/acadrust, in process)

rules.why: save_to serialises with the host's IoHooks.write (cadcraft_io::write picks DXF, DWG, SVG, PNG or PDF by the path's extension and DXF when there is none, so an extensionless path such as a dotfile gets DXF text), writes `<path>.cadcraft-tmp` with std::fs::write and renames it over `path`; qsave without `path` writes back to the path the drawing was opened from. Without hooks both fail before writing.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs: save_to (io() check, std::fs::write of the tmp file, std::fs::rename), run_save, run_saveas
crates/io/src/lib.rs: write() and ext() (an empty extension means DXF)

rules.why: run_wblock copies a block or the selected entities into a new drawing, serialises it with IoHooks.write and writes `path` directly with std::fs::write (not atomic, overwrites whatever is there).
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks.rs: run_wblock (io() check, then std::fs::write(&path, &bytes))

rules.why: Both run run_plot: the host's IoHooks.plot (cadcraft_io::plot) renders the layout to PDF bytes in memory, which go to `path` (std::fs::write of `<path>.cadcraft-tmp`, then rename) or come back as base64 `data`. Naming trap: PLOT never reaches a printer, plotter or spooler here; without the plot hook it reports that plotting is not available.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs: run_plot (io().and_then(|h| h.plot), std::fs::write + std::fs::rename when `path` is given)
crates/io/src/pdf.rs: plot builds the PDF in memory

rules.why: Only Session.docs and Session.active change: new pushes a fresh in-memory Drawing, close/closeall drop open drawings without saving (unsaved edits are lost), document.switch changes the active index.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs: run_new, run_close, run_closeall, run_switch
crates/engine/src/lib.rs: Session::new_drawing

rules.why: Serialises the open drawing with IoHooks.write into memory and returns it as base64; no path is read or written (it fails without the hook). The png/pdf/svg formats render through cadcraft_render, whose text layout may load installed system fonts by family name (see the text-style rule).
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs: run_bytes (hooks.write(doc, "drawing.<format>"), base64_encode)
crates/io/src/lib.rs: write() returns Vec<u8>

rules.why: The clipboard is engine-internal: copy_to_clip stores cloned entities in Session.clipboard (Vec<Entity>) with clipboard_base, paste/pasteorig add copies of them to the current space, cutclip also removes the originals. The OS clipboard is never touched (no clipboard crate in the engine or its dependencies).
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs: copy_to_clip, run_cut, paste, run_paste, run_pasteorig
crates/engine/src/lib.rs: Session { clipboard: Vec<Entity>, clipboard_base }

rules.why: Undo/redo swap Arc<Drawing> snapshots on DocState.undo/redo; the selection commands and quick select only change DocState.selection or query entities; erase.selection removes the selected entities from the drawing.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs: run_undo, run_redo, run_clear, run_selectall, run_select
crates/engine/src/cmd/qselect.rs: run_qselect, run_info
crates/engine/src/lib.rs: Session::undo, Session::redo

rules.why: View state is session or drawing data, not UI: zoom and pan call DocState::set_view, which keeps the view in DocState.views/view_history (session memory) or, inside an MSPACE viewport, in that Viewport entity's view_center/view_height; regen, regenall and redraw only call Session::touch (revision += 1); view.get reads the view and the viewport size the UI reported; layout.set switches DocState.space. Nothing reaches a window or the OS.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/view.rs: zoom, fit, pan_frac, run_pan, run_view_set, run_layout_set, the regen/regenall/redraw closures calling s.touch()
crates/engine/src/lib.rs: DocState::set_view/store_view, Session::touch, Session::zoom_extents

rules.why: Each builds entities from its JSON parameters and adds them to the current space (Session::add_entity); divide and measure place points or references to the drawing's own blocks. No I/O: the only std::fs calls in crates/engine are in file.rs, blocks.rs (wblock) and layout.rs (plot).
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs: run_line ... run_mtext

crates/engine/src/cmd/draw2.rs: run_arc_variant, run_circle_variant, run_circle_ttr/ttt, run_ellipse_axis/arc, run_divide, run_measure, run_revcloud, run_wipeout, run_3dpoly, run_mline, run_helix, run_spline_cv, run_centermark, run_centerline

rules.why: Dimensions, leaders, their overrides, association and text placement are entities and DimStyle data in the drawing; dimension geometry comes from cadcraft_render::dimension_geometry in memory.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate.rs: run_linear, run_aligned, run_radius, run_diameter, run_angular, run_arclen, run_ordinate, run_continue, run_baseline, run_qdim, run_mleader, run_leader, run_update, run_override, run_reassociate, run_disassociate, run_tedit, run_dimtedit, run_dimspace

rules.why: Hatch patterns come from the built-in table (cadcraft_doc::library::pattern), never a .pat file; boundaries and regions are computed from drawing entities; hatchedit forwards to the fixed properties.set command.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/hatch.rs: run_hatch, run_gradient, run_boundary, run_region, run_hatchedit (s.execute("properties.set", ...))
crates/doc/src/library.rs: standard_patterns, pattern

rules.why: Naming trap: insert places a reference to a block from the drawing's own block table (s.doc().block(name)) and never reads a DWG/DXF file the way AutoCAD's INSERT can; `explode: true` runs only the fixed explode command. block, attdef, attedit, base, purge, blocks.list and battman edit or list drawing tables.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks.rs: insert, run_insert (s.execute("explode", ...)), make_block, run_attdef, run_attedit, run_base, run_purge, run_list, run_battman

rules.why: Geometric edits of existing entities in the drawing (transforms, trim/extend, fillet/chamfer, arrays, polyline and spline edits, grip edits); copy and ncopy duplicate entities inside the drawing, not to any clipboard.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs: run_erase ... run_overkill
crates/engine/src/cmd/modify2.rs: run_pedit, run_splinedit, run_lengthen, run_align, run_blend, run_reverse, run_ncopy, run_chspace, run_flatten, run_arraypath, run_textedit
crates/engine/src/cmd/gripcmds.rs: run_grip_move/stretch/rotate/scale/mirror

rules.why: Layer table edits; layer states are kept in the drawing (Drawing.layer_states) and the LAYERP/LAYISO snapshots in CADCRAFT_* header variables, so nothing is imported from or exported to .las files.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/layer.rs: run_state_save/restore/list/delete/rename (d.layer_states), run_layerp, run_layiso, run_layuniso (header CADCRAFT_LAYERP, CADCRAFT_LAYISO)

rules.why: Layouts and paper-space viewports are drawing data and mspace/pspace set DocState.mspace; pagesetup stores page settings on the layout and keeps plotStyleTable as a plain string (no .ctb/.stb is ever loaded); layout dispatches to the fixed layout.* functions.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs: run_layout (find_command("layout.set")), run_new, run_delete, run_rename, run_copy, run_list, run_mview, run_mview_n, run_viewport_set, run_pagesetup, run_mspace, run_pspace
crates/doc/src/tables.rs: PageSetup.plot_style_table is only stored

rules.why: Entity properties, current-property header variables and style tables in the drawing; linetype `load` copies from the built-in cadcraft_doc::library::standard_linetypes, never a .lin file.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs: run_get, run_set, run_matchprop, run_color, run_linetype, run_lweight, run_ltscale, run_units, run_limits, run_style_current, run_dimstyle*, dim_override, run_tablestyle, run_mleaderstyle, run_ptype, run_rename
crates/doc/src/library.rs: standard_linetypes

rules.why: They edit or list Drawing.text_styles. Their reply's `trueType` flag calls cadcraft_fonts::TextFont::resolve, whose ttf::find scans fixed system font folders (/System/Library/Fonts, /Library/Fonts, ~/Library/Fonts; /usr/share/fonts, ~/.fonts, ~/.local/share/fonts; C:\Windows\Fonts) once per process and reads the matching .ttf/.otf by family name. The `font` value is a name key, never a path, so there is no caller path to confine; it only reveals which fonts are installed.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs: style_json (TextFont::resolve(&st.font).is_outline()), styles_json returned by run_style, run_style_list, run_style_rename, run_style_delete
crates/fonts/src/ttf.rs: scan() (read_dir of the fixed font folders), find() (std::fs::read of the matched file)
crates/fonts/src/lib.rs: TextFont::resolve

rules.why: Read-only queries of the drawing and session (distances, areas, entity listings, counts, a drawing summary with its title and path); time reports the revision counter, not a clock; id sets LASTPOINT in the session.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/inquiry.rs: run_dist, run_id, run_list, run_area, run_time, run_status, run_inspect, run_entities, run_count

rules.why: Drafting toggles and SETVAR change Session.settings (osmode, orthomode, gridmode ... qpmode) or Drawing.header variables, and getvar/sysvars read them. Settings live in session memory and neither the engine nor any cadcraft host persists them (no config writes anywhere), so this is in-memory session state, not an app preference; it would become host if a host started saving Session.settings.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/settings.rs: toggle, run_osnap, run_dsettings, run_setvar, run_getvar
crates/engine/src/sysvars.rs: get, set, list (SESSION_VARS or the drawing header)
crates/engine/src/lib.rs: Settings is a plain field of Session

rules.why: cal evaluates arithmetic with the engine's own bounded parser (10,000-character cap, depth limit, finite results), not a script interpreter; find/replace edits text entities in the current space; massprop and the measures compute geometry; measuregeom dispatches only to the fixed dist and area commands.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/utility.rs: eval/Parser, run_cal, run_find, run_massprop, run_measuregeom (s.execute("dist" | "area")), run_radius, run_angle

rules.why: Table entities and their cells in the drawing.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs: run_table, run_set, run_insert_row, run_delete_row, run_insert_col, run_delete_col, run_merge, run_unmerge

rules.why: Geometric and dimensional constraints, user parameters and their display settings live in Drawing.constraints/Drawing.parametric and are solved in process by cadcraft-constraints; `expr` values go through its arithmetic expression evaluator; constraint bars and dynamic dimensions are display flags stored in the drawing. The gc* and dc* ids are generated by the gc!/dc! macros.
evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/constraints.rs: gc!/dc! macros, run_gc, run_dc, run_geomconstraint, run_dimconstraint, run_autoconstrain, set_bars, bar_cmd, run_delconstraint, run_parameters, run_constraintsettings, run_inspect
crates/constraints/src/expr.rs: Env::eval
